title: Health Psychology Adventure 3: Health Belief Model & TPB
welcome_lead: Today you'll predict behaviour with the Health Belief Model and the Theory of Planned Behaviour.
meta_desc: Psychology Health: Health Belief Model (Rosenstock 1966) and Theory of Planned Behaviour (Ajzen 1985).
final_note: You compared two models of health-related decision making.

concepts.def: Belief one can perform the behaviour

walkthroughs.body_html:
Irwin Rosenstock (1966) explained why people do (or don't) act on health advice.

Behaviour depends on:
- Perceived susceptibility
- Perceived severity
- Perceived benefits
- Perceived barriers
- Cues to action
- Self-efficacy (added later)

Used to design vaccination, screening and smoking campaigns.

Icek Ajzen (1985) extended the Theory of Reasoned Action.

Intention predicts behaviour, formed from:
- Attitudes toward the behaviour.
- Subjective norms (what important others think).
- Perceived behavioural control (can I do this?).

Both models are cognitive — emotion and habit get little weight.

Intention-behaviour gap: knowing what to do doesn't guarantee doing it (Webb & Sheeran, 2006).

Implementation intentions ('if X then I'll do Y', Gollwitzer 1999) help close the gap.
